objectives.statement: Use man as a subject-only generic pronoun and en or ens where object or possessive forms are needed.
Distinguish the tone of generic du and colloquial folk from more neutral generic choices.
Build natural Bokmål sentences with consistent generic pronoun choice.
Recognize when a pronoun refers to people in general rather than a specific person.

notes: Must contrast generic man, en, du, and folk by grammar and register. Include that man is subject-only, en can be object/possessive, du is informal/generic in speech, and folk is colloquial.
